Verdict: REVISE — major revision requiredThe charge arithmetic and the proposed slot totals are internally consistent, but the proof does not establish the crucial inequality
$$K_{\mathrm{irregular}}+G
\le 2S+2B_{01}+2B_{10}.
\tag{2}$$
Consequently, the displayed lower bound
$$\sigma\ge N-S-2B_{01}-2B_{10}+C
\tag{3}$$
and the sufficient conditions (4)–(5) remain conditional on an unproved injection and an unproved disjointness claim. I did not use the finite checker or the accompanying Lean controls.The theorem may be salvageable, but the current written argument is not sufficient for acceptance.What is correct, conditional on the missing injectionSeveral parts of the package are sound once the local slot theorem is supplied as an additional lemma.The source charges and the definition of  $S$  give
$$\sum_i \rho_i=N-S.$$
Given the stated ledger
$$\sigma\ge N+S+C-K_{\mathrm{irregular}}-G,
\tag{1}$$
the claimed implication from (2) is arithmetically correct:
$$\begin{aligned}
\sigma
&\ge N+S+C-\bigl(2S+2B_{01}+2B_{10}\bigr)\\
&=N-S-2B_{01}-2B_{10}+C.
\end{aligned}$$
The width expansion in (5) is also correct:each phase- $(0,1)$  source contributes  $3$ ;each phase- $(1,0)$  source contributes  $w+1$ ;each phase- $(1,1)$  source contributes  $w-1$ ;each charge-minus-two rotor contributes  $2$ .Likewise, the displayed pool sizes agree with the proposed right-hand side of (2):
$$4B_{01}
+\sum_{\mathrm{phase}\,10}2w_i
+\sum_{\mathrm{phase}\,11}(2w_i-2)
+4R_{\mathrm{minus}}
=
2S+2B_{01}+2B_{10}.$$
The phase table also appears numerically consistent if its intended definitions are supplied precisely. The problem is the justification that every actual side loss and every actual irregular event occupies those pools exactly once.1. The definition of  $X$  is ambiguous, and its literal reading contradicts the tableThe text defines a continuation exception by saying that an endpoint  $p$  has“some adjacent intratile ORIGINAL blank  $v$  has other intratile neighbor  $u$  such that  $2p-u$  is not an original endpoint.”Grammatically, this says that  $u$  is another intratile neighbor of  $v$ . Under that reading, the phase- $(0,0)$  assertion  $X=\varnothing$  is false.For example, take  $w=6$ ,  $a=b=4$ , phase  $(0,0)$ , and
$$p=(1,1).$$
Then  $p$  is an original endpoint in the tile  $\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}$ . The site
$$v=(1,0)$$
is an adjacent intratile original blank. The other intratile neighbor of  $v$  is
$$u=(0,0),$$
which is a selected site in the source. But
$$2p-u=(2,2),$$
and  $(2,2)$  is not an original endpoint. Thus  $p\in X$  under the literal wording, whereas the table asserts  $X=\varnothing$ .The phase table becomes consistent only under a different definition:  $u$  must be the other intratile neighbor of  $p$ , distinct from the blank neighbor  $v$ . That intended definition needs to be stated formally. The subsequent proof also uses that interpretation when it speaks of “the other intratile neighbor” of  $t$ .This is a repairable definition problem, but as written the catalogue is not a valid lemma.2.  $E$ ,  $X$ , and  $I$  must be defined source-locallyThe proof later uses  $E_i$ ,  $X_i$ , and the joint pool of source  $i$ , but the definitions in Section 2 are stated globally:“For each original endpoint  $p$ , call it an exterior exception if it has no original endpoint neighbor OUTSIDE its physical tile.”That is not compatible with the argument in Section 3 unless “original endpoint neighbor” means an endpoint belonging to the same source module. For example, when a foreign endpoint enters the positive gate  $u$ , the sites  $(1,2)$  and  $(2,1)$  are original endpoints of the fixed positive source and lie outside  $u$ 's physical tile. Under a global definition,  $u$  would have outside original endpoint neighbors and would not be in  $E_i$ . Under the intended source-local definition, those endpoints belong to a different source and do not count.The theorem should explicitly define, for each source  $i$ ,
$$E_i,\quad X_i,\quad I_i$$
using the original endpoint set  $P_i$ , rather than the global endpoint union. The same source-local convention is needed for the continuation-reflection test and for the claim that an assigned endpoint lies in its owner’s pool.3. The blank-gate assignment does not prove that the selected endpoint comes from the required poolThis is the most serious gap in Section 3.In the blank-gate case, the argument is: $u$  is not an endpoint and remains blank.A marked side has  $v$  or  $z$  as an endpoint.If  $v$  is an endpoint, the old selection
$$x=(3,2)$$
cannot remain selected because it has occupied neighbors  $p=(3,1)$  and  $v$ .Therefore at least one of  $x,z$  is an endpoint.Choose one such endpoint  $t$ , let  $i$  be its owner, and infer  $t\in X_i$ .The last inference is not justified.The site  $x$  is an original selection of the fixed positive phase- $(0,0)$  module, not an original endpoint in that module. The hypotheses say:“Retain the union of all supports except those becoming endpoints.”Thus, if  $x$  acquires too many occupied neighbors, the stated rules appear to allow  $x$  to be reclassified as a final endpoint. Nothing in the hypotheses forbids promoted selections from becoming endpoints. If  $x$  is the only endpoint among  $\{x,z\}$ , then:its owner is the positive phase- $(0,0)$  module; $x\notin P_i$ , so  $X_i$  is not even defined for it;even if  $X_i$  were extended to promoted selections, the phase- $(0,0)$  catalogue has  $X=\varnothing$ .The fixed positive endpoint  $p=(3,1)$  and guard  $q=(1,3)$  do not create a continuation exception for  $x$ ; they are endpoints of the same positive source. The statement“If  $t$  had continuation ... those belong to the fixed positive owner. Therefore  $t\in X_i$ ”only works if  $i$  is already known to be a different source and  $t$  is known to be an original endpoint of that source. Neither fact is established.The final-degree hypothesis does not automatically repair this. If  $x$  is promoted to an endpoint, it needs at least three occupied neighbors; in the blank-gate situation it already has  $p$  and  $v$ , and an additional site such as  $y=(3,3)$  could in principle be occupied by another endpoint. The submitted hypotheses do not contain an invariant excluding that configuration.A valid proof needs one of the following:a lemma that original selections such as  $x$  can never be promoted to endpoints in the stated fusion class;a lemma that in the blank-gate case the endpoint among  $x,z$  must be a foreign original endpoint, never  $x$ ;or an expanded slot catalogue that includes promoted selections and changes the capacity bound.Without such a lemma, the asserted injection into  $A_i\cup F_i$  is not proved.4. The proof does not establish that every marked witness is an endpointThe marked-side definition is:“Marked iff any protector gains a neighbor.”For the protector at  $(4,1)$ , the relevant old blank is
$$v=(4,2).$$
Unlike  $u$  and  $z$ ,  $v$  is not visibly adjacent to an old positive endpoint: its local neighbors include  $x=(3,2)$ , which is an old selection, and blank sites. The stated rule“Every new occupied old blank adjacent to an old endpoint is a foreign endpoint”therefore does not by itself imply that an occupied  $v$  is an endpoint.If a foreign source contributes a selection at  $v$ , that selection could initially be retained, promoted, or interact with  $x$ ; the proof never analyzes these cases. There may be a repair using the unique source anchor of a foreign selection: a foreign selection at  $v$  has its own occupied endpoint anchor, and  $v$  is adjacent to  $x$ , so retaining  $v$  as a selection may violate the one-occupied-neighbor rule. But that argument must be written and must be combined with the possible promotion of  $x$ . It is not a consequence of the currently stated “old blank adjacent to old endpoint” rule.Thus the proof has not shown that each marked side can even be assigned an endpoint, much less an endpoint in  $E_i\cup X_i$ .5. The shared-slot exclusion is asserted without the necessary event characterizationThe only stated relationship between  $I$  and  $K_{\mathrm{irregular}}$  is:“Every irregular event uses one distinct endpoint in  $I$ .”That is a one-way containment. It does not say that an endpoint in  $I$  produces an irregular event exactly when its particular intratile blank is occupied, nor that no other interaction can produce an irregular event at that endpoint.The shared-pool issue occurs for a phase- $(1,1)$  upper corner  $A$ : $A\subset I$ ; $A$  is a possible side slot in the blank-gate case;the proof says that because the gate  $u$  remains blank, the corner incurs no irregular event.The implication
$$u\text{ remains blank}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\text{no irregular event owned by }A$$
does not follow from the definitions in the attachment. The fact that the endpoint has one intratile blank and an irregular  $2P0T$  receiver profile only places it in  $I$ ; it does not define the actual event trigger.To make this part valid, the earlier irregular-ledger result must be imported in the following explicit form, or reproved here:every  $K_{\mathrm{irregular}}$  event has a unique owner in  $I_i$ ;an owner  $p\in I_i$  can incur its event only through occupation or alteration of its designated intratile blank;no other contact, endpoint promotion, or source overlap can create a second event at  $p$ ;when  $p\in A$  is used as a blank-gate side slot, that designated blank is exactly  $u$ , so the event is absent.Without this strengthened event lemma, the claimed disjointness of the side assignments and irregular-event assignments is not established.6. The rotor part does not cure the non-rotor gapsGranting the stated rotor barrier, it is reasonable to exclude rotor endpoints from the gate  $u$ , and from  $x$  or  $z$  when  $u$  is blank. That handles the rotor portion of the proposed pool.It does not address:a promoted old selection  $x$ ;a foreign selected site at  $v$ ;the source-local meaning of  $E_i$  and  $X_i$ ;or the actual trigger for an irregular event.Those are all non-rotor issues, so the rotor barrier cannot complete the injection argument by itself.Required revisionsBefore the theorem can be accepted, the proof should add the following explicit components.A. Formal source-local definitionsFor every source  $i$ , define  $E_i$ ,  $X_i$ , and  $I_i$  relative to  $P_i$ , and state unambiguously that in the definition of  $X_i$ ,  $u$  is the other intratile neighbor of  $p$ , not another neighbor of  $v$ .B. A complete marked-side endpoint lemmaProve that every marked side has a selected witness  $t$  satisfying
$$t\in P_i\cap(E_i\cup X_i)$$
for some foreign source  $i$ , and that  $t$  is an original endpoint of that source. This proof must handle:occupation of  $v$  by an endpoint;occupation of  $v$  by a foreign selection;promotion of the fixed selection  $x$ ;the possibility that  $z$  is blank;and the final endpoint degree requirement.If promoted selections are allowed, they must either be ruled out in this local configuration or added to the slot catalogue.C. A rigorous irregular-event ownership lemmaProve the exact condition under which an  $I_i$ -endpoint contributes to  $K_{\mathrm{irregular}}$ , including the phase- $(1,1)$  upper-corner case. The blankness of  $u$  must be connected explicitly to the absence of the corresponding event.D. Only then redo the disjoint-pool countAfter A–C, the pool sum in Section 4 can be used to prove (2). Until then, it is only a count of available candidate positions, not a count of actual demand.Final assessmentThe theorem’s numerical formulas and conditional arithmetic are coherent. The phase catalogue is also plausibly correct under an intended, narrower interpretation of  $X$ . However, the submitted proof has two central unproved assertions:every marked side has an injectively assignable foreign original-endpoint slot; and  the side-slot assignment is disjoint from actual irregular-event ownership.Because those assertions are exactly what establish (2), the theorem is not proved in its current form. The appropriate verdict is REVISE, with the revisions above treated as substantive proof obligations rather than editorial clarification.
